title: Shrimp Shish Kabob with Vegetables, No Potatoes

content.title: About
content.content: The shrimp shish kabob with vegetables, no potatoes, is a grilled skewer where large shrimp alternate with chunks of bell pepper, zucchini, onion and cherry tomatoes. All ingredients are marinated in olive oil, lemon juice, garlic and spices, then threaded onto skewers and grilled until lightly charred.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Shrimp are one of the fastest‑growing seafood species, farmed in as little as 3–4 months.
Seafood kebabs are a staple of Mediterranean cuisine, often featuring olive oil and fresh herbs.
Omitting potatoes makes the dish lighter and lowers its glycemic index.
Shrimp get their pink hue from astaxanthin, a powerful antioxidant.
Grilling vegetables quickly retains most of their vitamins compared to prolonged cooking.

items.title: High in protein
items.content: Shrimp provide about 20 g of protein per 100 g, supporting muscle maintenance.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: Most of the fat in shrimp is polyunsaturated, and the overall fat content is modest.

items.title: Source of iodine and selenium
items.content: These trace minerals are essential for thyroid function and antioxidant defense.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: Shrimp contain vitamin B12, niacin and riboflavin, which aid energy metabolism.

items.title: Antioxidants from vegetables
items.content: Bell peppers and tomatoes are rich in vitamin C and lycopene, boosting immunity.

items.title: Shellfish allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience severe allergic reactions to shrimp.

items.title: Cholesterol content
items.content: Shrimp contain cholesterol, so people with hypercholesterolemia should monitor portion size.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Improper storage or undercooking can allow bacterial growth leading to food poisoning.

items.title: Salt in the marinade
items.content: Excessive salt can raise blood pressure in salt‑sensitive individuals.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the kabob hot, straight off the grill. Eat directly from the skewer, cut into bite‑size pieces for salads, rice or couscous dishes, and pair with a light yogurt or tzatziki sauce.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2 days. For longer keeping, freeze in freezer‑safe bags for up to 1 month. Reheat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
